cohort: The study included 38 pregnant women (19 with Sickle Cell Disease and 19 controls without SCD) from the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital's labour unit.
finding: Placentae from women with Sickle Cell Disease exhibited statistically significant increases in syncytial knot formation, foetal capillaries, syncytial denuded areas, and reduced intervillous spaces compared to placentae from non-SCD women.
cross-section timing: Placenta samples were taken at term (38 weeks + 2 weeks).
